Central Truth: God personally and specially created mankind.

Catechism Q: What does "made in the image of God" mean?
Central Truth: God made mankind unique; we have some of God's own characteristics.
God created man to rule the earth and glorify him.
God made man with both a physical body and an immaterial soul.

Catechism Q: Why did God make men and women?
Central Truth: God made men and women to each fulfill distinct roles.

Catechism Q: Why did God create ethnicity and nations?
Central Truth: God created ethnicity and nations to glorify himself.

Catechism Q: Why did God institute human government?
Central Truth: God instituted human government to provide social order in the world.
Adam deliberately chose to disobey God.
Sin is any failure to meet God's perfect standard.

Catechism Q: How did Adam's sin affect all of mankind after him?
Central Truth: Adam's original sin means all human beings have sinful natures.

Catechism Q: How dows sin affect man's relationships?
Central Truth: Man's relationships with God
Bonus Verse: and creation are cursed because of sin.

Central Truth: Death is the judgment of a holy and just God on sinners.

Catechism Q: Can man please God and save himself?
Central Truth: Man has no ability to please God and save himself.

Catechism Q: What does God's choice in election mean?
Central Truth: God chose whose who would receive salvation and its blessings.

Catechism Q: What does the atonement tell us about God?
Central Truth: God is just and loving; he is righteous and merciful.

Catechism Q: Why is Christ's death called a sacrifice?
Central Truth: Jesus died as a sacrifice to be God's perfect substitute for elect sinners.

Catechism Q: What did Christ's sacrifice do for those who believe?
Central Truth: Jesus' sacrificial death satisfied God's wrath.
Christ's blood was shed as the ransom payment for the sins of the elect.

Catechism Q: How does Jesus' death bring reconciliation?
Central Truth: Jesus' death brings peace between God and his people.
Christ's resurrection proves the gospel true and life giving.

Catechism Q: To whom does God offer salvation?
Central Truth: Gos issues his gracious call of salvation to all mankind.
Regeneration is a special work of the Holy Spirit giving life to dead sinners.
Sinners repent by turning to God from sin with their whole heart and life.
Faith is a whole-hearted commitment and trust in Jesus alone for salvation.
Those who have faith in Jesus have died with Christ and they now live in Christ.
Those who have faith in Jesus are declared to be righteous before God.
Sanctification is God's ongoing process of making all Christians more and more holy.
God assures believers of future glory; in hope of which Christians live obediently on earth.
Glorification is the transformation of the bodies and souls of believers to be like Christ.
